nba_directive.reason_text: This client has a 2.99% first mortgage — a rate that almost certainly cannot be improved by refinancing — so the winning move is Fed-vs-mortgage education to correct any rate-threshold misconception, while protecting their existing low rate and pivoting to a HELOC/second lien if equity access is the real need. Anchoring to their specific $1,011/mo payment and $208,492 balance makes the education concrete and credible.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by naming their rate and immediately validating why they're waiting
  - 'You're sitting at 2.99% — that's a rate worth protecting, full stop'
  - Acknowledge the instinct to wait for the Fed before making any move

- Deliver the Fed-vs-mortgage education as a credibility move, not a lecture
  - Explain that mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury, not the Fed Funds Rate
  - Key point: anticipated Fed cuts are already priced into today's mortgage rates — waiting for Fed action often means the rate move already happened
  - This reframe alone separates you from 95% of bankers who just say 'let me know when you're ready'

- Redirect the refinance conversation honestly: a rate-and-term refi on a 2.99% loan almost certainly doesn't pencil
  - Pull up their $1,011/mo P&I on $208,492 remaining — show them what a new rate would have to be just to break even, then let the math speak
  - Coach them: 'I'd rather tell you the truth than sell you a refi that costs you money'

- If the underlying need is cash or debt payoff, pivot to a HELOC/second lien — leave the 2.99% first mortgage completely untouched
  - Frame the HELOC rate against credit card rates (25–30%) not against their first mortgage
  - If they carry any revolving balances, ask for the balances now so you can run real consolidation savings math — do not invent a number, compute it from what they share
  - Monthly savings from eliminating high-rate card debt is the anchor, not the HELOC rate itself

- Carry a break-even timeline for any scenario you present
  - For a refi: closing costs ÷ monthly savings = months to break even (compute live, don't estimate)
  - For a HELOC: show the monthly cash-flow improvement from day one if consolidating debt

- Secure a specific next step before closing the text thread
  - Offer a 10-minute call to run the actual numbers together
  - Or send a soft-pull link so you can price a real scenario — 'no commitment, just real numbers so you can decide with full information'
  - Do not leave the thread open-ended; name the time or the link
